evidence.title: 日下舊聞考 正大光明
evidence.excerpt_zh: 大宫門内為出入賢良門五楹門左右為直房前跨石橋度橋東西朝房各五楹西南為茶膳房再西為繙書房東南為清茶房為軍機處（圓明園冊）臣等謹按出入賢良門額世宗御書是為二宫門凡武職侍衛引見御此門較射左右直房為各部院臣工入直之所東西設兩罩門各衙門奏事由東罩門逓進茶膳房太監人等由西罩門出入門前河形如月中駕石橋三其水自西來東注如意門閘口㑹東園各河而出出入賢良門内為正大光明殿七楹東西配殿各五楹後為壽山殿東為洞明堂（圓明園冊）臣等謹按圓明園四十景中世宗御題四字額者凡十有四正大光明殿其一也餘如牡丹臺今為鏤月開雲蓬萊洲今為蓬島瑶臺乃乾隆九年皇上恭依避暑山莊三十六景四字題額之例更鍚嘉名用昭畫一敬就各條下加按並恭載御製四十景詩至附近各景詩已載御製詩全集者兹不備録又按正大光明殿内聨曰心天之心而宵衣旰食樂民之樂以和性怡情為世宗御書又聨曰遹求寜觀成無逺弗届以對時育物有那其居為皇上御書東壁懸御書周書無逸篇西壁懸豳風圖東為洞明堂世宗御書額
evidence.summary: Through the five-bay 出入賢良門, the second gate with duty rooms and three stone bridges over a moon-shaped canal, are court offices, kitchens, the translation office and the 軍機處 Grand Council. Then 正大光明殿 of seven bays with five-bay side halls, 壽山殿 behind and 洞明堂 to the east. The notes explain the renaming of the fourteen Yongzheng titles under the 1744 four-character scheme, and record the couplets, the 無逸 text on the east wall and the 豳風 picture on the west wall.

evidence.excerpt_zh: 圆明园章京直庐，一在挂甲屯，一在冰窖。
evidence.summary: Grand Council secretaries of the garden had two lodgings outside it, at 掛甲屯 and 冰窖.

evidence.title: Scene 1, 正大光明 Zhengda Guangming: courts, gate, moat and hall
evidence.excerpt_other: This Second Gate of the Palace led into the courtyard where the Main Audience Hall stood on a foundation 129 feet long, 63 feet wide, and 4 feet high, ascended by three sets of stone steps. It was a building of seven chien besides having a porch all around the outside, formed by an outer row of columns supporting the projecting eaves, so that the facade presented a colonnade of ten columns.
evidence.summary: Malone measured the site. Foundation 129 x 63 x 4 ft, three stairs, seven bays plus a surrounding porch, ten columns across the front, round column bases 2 ft 9 in across, floor of veined marble slabs on brick and lime. Plain under Yongzheng in 1725; before the end of Qianlong's reign columns red, capitals with dragons, gilt wire over the entablature. Pines and a rockery hill behind, a covered passage to the east.

evidence.title: The Great Palace Gate and the offices before it
evidence.excerpt_other: The Great Palace Gate was a roofed building in which hung a tablet inscribed with the name of the garden, Yuan Ming Yuan, written by the Emperor K'ang Hsi.
evidence.summary: 大宫门 Da Gongmen: waiting rooms beside the road, behind them offices of the boards and the Eight Banners, the Grand Council, the 南书房 imperial school, treasury, dispensary and kitchens. Note 15 on p.70 lists the offices east and west of the gate by name.

evidence.title: 论清代圆明园军机处 (何瑜)
evidence.summary: 何瑜 reviews the rival dates for the founding of the Grand Council and argues it began in spring 1729 and, by location, in 圆明园 itself, for the western campaign.
